base_prompt: Create ONE Bug Archive episode mascot, matching all ten supplied first-episode reference images as STYLE REFERENCES only. Polished smooth 2D anime sticker, fluorescent yellow-lime rounded soft bug, two long thin antennae with big round bulbs, huge black oval shiny eyes, rosy cheeks, tiny feet, dark plum fine outline, upper-left white gloss. Entire bug and props visible, centered with clear margin. A single clear visual gag expresses the compiler error, integrated into its costume/body/prop; readable at thumbnail size. Genuinely transparent PNG. No text, letters, numbers, code, labels, card, scene, floor, cast shadow, watermark. Do not make a collage. Error concept:

episodes.concept: Partial declarations use inconsistent type parameter names: one bug trying to clasp two matching jacket halves, but each half has a different identity badge, a cyan star versus a purple crescent. Bug compares the contradictory badges with worried expression. Emphasize matching halves but mismatched identity emblems.

Partial modifier in wrong position: a bug with a puzzle shell wearing its detachable puzzle connector awkwardly on top of its antenna instead of at the visibly empty matching shell seam. It points toward the correct empty seam, puzzled.

Partial method inside a non-partial class: bug holds a small jigsaw-shaped gear up to its solid seamless shell, which has no matching split or connector to receive it. Tiny gear clearly cannot be installed.

Implementation without a defining declaration: builder bug holds a finished toy gear mechanism over a completely empty outline-shaped blueprint frame, confused that there is no defining pattern. No written marks.
Duplicate partial method definitions: bug holds two identical hollow outline-only gear stencils competing for one empty gear-shaped slot on its belly. Both stencils empty, not working solid gears.

Duplicate partial method implementations: bug has two identical solid working wind-up gears trying to occupy a single mounting axle on its belly, jammed together. Solid filled gears and double crank handles make duplicate implementations obvious.

Ambiguous inherited member: bug between two identical little jewel buttons on a split shoulder harness, each connected from a different side, finger hovering indecisively between the indistinguishable buttons.

Trying to call a field like a method: bug desperately tries to turn a crank attached to a plain solid heart-shaped health gem on its belly; the gem has no machinery or socket and the loose crank fails to engage.

Inherited methods collapse to same signature after generic substitution: bug holds two differently colored keys whose tooth patterns are EXACTLY identical, both jammed side by side at one tiny keyhole on its shell.

Overloads differ only by ref/out/in: bug wears two identical toy blasters with exactly identical connector plugs, distinguished only by opposing tiny pictorial arrows on their straps; both compete for one holster.
